findings.finding: bms_master condition coverage gap = 1.10% (ASIL D, limit 0%)
findings.reasoning: Condition coverage is the per-operand cousin of decision coverage: every Boolean sub-expression must take both true and false values. Gaps usually indicate dead operands inside compound predicates.
recommend: Inspect the AND/OR fan-in of the failing predicate; reorder or simplify when one operand is provably invariant.

findings.finding: bms_master decision coverage gap = 2.80% (ASIL D, limit 0%)
findings.reasoning: Decision coverage is highly recommended for ASIL D. A non-zero gap means at least one if/Switch/relational has only been exercised in one direction by MIL.
recommend: Coverage Report > Decision metric: each '<100%' decision lists which outcome (true/false) is missing.
Add the missing-direction stimulus to MIL, or filter the decision with a §9.4.5 rationale (typically a defensive branch that cannot occur on the integration target).

findings.finding: bms_master execution coverage gap = 0.50% (ASIL D, limit 0%)
findings.reasoning: Statement coverage at the model level is the easiest metric to close; any gap on an ASIL-D component means at least one block is structurally unreachable from the MIL stimulus -- either dead code to delete or a missing test case.
recommend: Open Simulink Coverage > Coverage Report and sort blocks by execution; the unhit ones are the offenders.
Either delete unreachable blocks, or add a MIL test that drives them and re-run mil.run.

findings.finding: bms_master MC/DC coverage gap = 90.20% (ASIL D, limit 5%)
findings.reasoning: MC/DC is highly recommended for ASIL D. Each independent operand of every decision must demonstrate that it can flip the outcome on its own. Achieving 100% on legacy logic is rarely practical; ISO 26262-6 §9.4.5 explicitly allows incomplete coverage if the gap is justified -- this rule fires above 5% so the remaining cases get a written rationale rather than silently ignored.
recommend: For each uncovered MC/DC pair, decide between (a) adding a driving stimulus, (b) refactoring the predicate to remove masked operands, or (c) accepting the gap with a §9.4.5 justification recorded in the safety case.

findings.reasoning: `bms_master/Estimation/SOC_Loop` participates in an algebraic loop. Such loops are non-deterministic on the embedded target -- Simulink Coder will either refuse to generate code or insert a runtime solver call that no WCET budget can absorb.
recommend: Insert a `Unit Delay` (or `Memory`) block on the back edge of the loop that includes `bms_master/Estimation/SOC_Loop`, breaking the direct-feedthrough dependency. Re-run `sldiagnostics(<model>, 'AlgebraicLoops')` to confirm.

findings.reasoning: `bms_master/Library_Wrappers/CellLib_Adapter` references a library Simulink cannot resolve (status = unresolved). Code generation will either fail or build against a stale shadow of the library master -- both unacceptable for an ASIL-D component because the resulting binary no longer matches the model that was reviewed.
recommend: Restore the parent library on the MATLAB path, then right-click `bms_master/Library_Wrappers/CellLib_Adapter` > Library Link > Resolve Library Links.
If the library is intentionally retired, replace `bms_master/Library_Wrappers/CellLib_Adapter` with the in-model implementation and remove the link.

findings.reasoning: `bms_master/L1/L2/L3/L4/L5/L6/L7/L8/L9/Const` lives 9 subsystem levels deep. Beyond 5 levels review and Coverage instrumentation slow down and the added boundaries usually carry no abstraction value.
recommend: Promote `bms_master/L1/L2/L3/L4/L5/L6/L7/L8/L9/Const` one or two levels by collapsing the intermediate Subsystem boundary that adds no abstraction.

findings.reasoning: McCabe complexity 47 on `bms_master/Protection/Fault_Manager` puts MC/DC closure out of practical reach (each new linearly-independent path adds at least one required test case). Above ~30 the unit is also too dense for a single-pass code review.
recommend: Split `bms_master/Protection/Fault_Manager` along its top-level decision points (e.g. mode multiplexers, fault arbiters); aim for cyclomatic ≤ 10 per resulting subsystem.

findings.finding: Stateflow chart `Master_FSM` at bms_master/Mode_Manager/Master_FSM has 55 states (limit 20)
findings.reasoning: Chart `Master_FSM` carries 55 states (above the 20-state guideline). Charts this size are the dominant source of MC/DC gaps in fault-handling logic and are difficult to review on a single screen.
recommend: Refactor `Master_FSM` into hierarchical sub-charts grouped by mode (e.g. Init / Run / Fault / Shutdown); each sub-chart should hold ≤ 20 states.

findings.reasoning: `bms_master/Estimation/SOC_Estimator` is an atomic subsystem holding 145 direct children, well above the 100-block guideline. Atomic units this large are the dominant driver of cyclomatic complexity and MC/DC gaps in BMS code, and become the bottleneck in code review.
recommend: Split `bms_master/Estimation/SOC_Estimator` into 2-3 smaller atomic subsystems grouped by responsibility (e.g. estimation / protection / housekeeping).

findings.reasoning: The schedule has 5 distinct rates (4 is the guideline). Beyond that, the generated code's task table grows and WCET analysis becomes pessimistic because rare slow tasks have to be assumed worst-case in every base period.
recommend: Display > Sample Time > Colors to inspect the legend, then consolidate close-by rates onto a common base or isolate slow paths behind explicit Rate Transition blocks.

findings.reasoning: `bms_master/Signal_Aggregator/Decode_Fault_Flags/Logical Operator` is a Logic inside `bms_master/Signal_Aggregator/Decode_Fault_Flags`; its Inport port #2 is not wired. On an ASIL-D component an unwired interface is an ambiguity in the architectural design: code generation will pick a default (zero / Ground) that is invisible from the diagram and that no review can confirm matches the requirement.
recommend: Either route the intended signal into Inport port #2 of `bms_master/Signal_Aggregator/Decode_Fault_Flags/Logical Operator`, or close it explicitly with a Ground / Terminator so the design intent is documented.
